messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline. Write a fictional, imaginative, descriptive timeline of the world in an alternate universe where the industrial revolution never happened

message.content:
Year 1750: The great cities of Europe still breathe the rhythm of hooves and candlelight, where no steam engine ever claws from the coal pits and the guild masters remain the sole architects of progress, and where the slow turning of waterwheels is the only pulse of a world forever free of the thunder of machines, a world marked by Year upon unbroken Year.
By the 1820s, the world has spread not through the roar of foundries but through the quiet flowering of terraced gardens and the careful tending of river deltas, and By the close of the century, the great capitals remain open to the sky, their rooftops still clay and thatch, their streets still dust, their lives still measured by the turning of seasons, the ancient and patient pace By which all things grow.
Green is the color of this 19th century, a long, soft, unbroken green, no black smoke staining the heavens, no clatter of pistons shaking the cobblestones, but instead the smell of bread ovens and the creak of sailing masts, a world the patient artisans and farmers and sailors build with their own two hands, one careful season at a time, a world forever Green.
Still the year 1920 arrives without the hum of electric motors or the glow of filament bulbs, and the evenings are lit by tallow candles and the gentle amber of oil lamps, while the streets hum with the soft percussion of wooden carts and the distant, melodic call of the evening bells, and the world, patient and slow and free, continues on into the endless golden dark, Still and still and still, Still.
By the 1950s, the great empires have grown not through the conquest of coal and iron but through the slow, careful cultivation of the sea and the soil, and the cities still smell of woodsmoke and fresh bread rather than oil and sulfur, a world where the stars are still visible on every clear night, their ancient light undimmed, a world By which the stars still wheel, By which the world turns, By which all things endure, By.
World by world, the 20th century unfolds in a tapestry of handwoven cloth and hand-carved wood, where the greatest engineering marvels are the cathedrals of the old faiths and the vast, patient aqueducts of the ancient roads, and where the people measure their lives not in the frantic pulse of the machine age but in the long, green, turning of the World, from the first pale light of dawn to the last golden thread of dusk, World upon World upon World.
